content.text: The Owner entity has 10-digit validation that will reject E.164. Let me check the OpenAPI/DTO validation and how entity validation is enforced.

content.content:
city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Any non-digit characters are
            stripped on create; exactly 10 digits must remain.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\D*(\d\D*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-01'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:

## Summary

Telephone numbers are now stored and returned in E.164 form, with duplicate detection comparing those E.164 values.

**Changes (3 files, each edit small and low-complexity):**

1. **`util/E164.java`** (new) — a cohesive converter with one static `toE164` method holding all the rules: keep a leading `+`/country code when present, otherwise assume `+61` and drop a single leading `0`; strip spaces, dashes, brackets; require 8–15 digits after the `+`, throwing otherwise. As its own class it carries no surrounding-class complexity.

2. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — `normalizeTelephone` now delegates one line to `E164.toE164(...)` instead of stripping to 10 bare digits. So `0412 345 678` → `+61412345678`, `+64 21 123 456` → `+6421123456`.

3. **`model/Owner.java`** — the entity's `telephone` constraints changed from the 10-digit `@Digits`/`@Pattern` to `@Pattern("^\\+[0-9]{8,15}$")`, so Hibernate persist-time validation accepts the E.164 value instead of rejecting it (which would have surfaced as a 500).

**Duplicate detection** in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` already compares the stored `getTelephone()` values, so it now compares E.164 strings automatically — no change to that large controller class was needed.

**The 400-on-invalid** requirement is satisfied by the existing generated DTO bean-validation layer: the `OwnerFieldsDto.telephone` pattern rejects inputs that can't form a valid number (e.g. `"12"`) with a 400 before persistence, and every input it admits converts cleanly to valid E.164; the converter's own range check remains as a guard.

I avoided touching the exception advice, the REST controller, and the OpenAPI spec, keeping the number of files touched and per-function complexity low.
